div.p: To find nodes in an XML file with XPath, write expressions in a query file, an XPath editor below the XML file, and run them one at a time. The nodes an expression finds are listed as VS Code lists references, to step through in the XML file. Other results, such as a count or a list of strings, are shown after the expression.

figcaption.i: Enter XPaths in the query window to navigate the matching nodes.

div.aside: Requirements: SaxonJ - any edition, including Saxon-HE - set with the XSLT.tasks.saxonJar setting, and a Java runtime on the PATH. With Saxon-PE or Saxon-EE, expressions can use XPath 4.0 syntax. With Saxon-HE, they're XPath 3.1.
div.p: In the editor of an XML file, click the search button in the editor's title bar, or run XML: Find Nodes with XPath... - from the Command Palette, the XML Selection submenu of the editor's context menu, or the XML: Select Element... quick pick (⇧⌘2 / Ctrl+Shift+2).

The query file, queries.xpath, opens in an editor group below the XML file, a quarter of its height. A new query file starts with an expression for the XML file's root element, such as /orders. There's one query file for each workspace, kept by VS Code, so your expressions are there next time.
div.aside: With no folder open, there's one query file shared by all the VS Code windows without a folder.
div.p: The query file has several expressions, separated by blank lines. An expression can take several lines, with no blank line within it, and can have comments, (: like this :).

As in any XPath file, expressions are highlighted and checked as you type, and auto-completion includes the names of the elements and attributes in the XML file. Each expression is checked on its own.
The namespaces declared on the XML file's root element can be used without declaring them:

ul.li: a name without a prefix matches an element in the root element's default namespace - so for <orders xmlns="urn:orders">, //order finds its order elements
a prefix declared on the root element, e.g. xmlns:x="urn:extra", can be used as it is: //x:note

div.p: For another namespace - one first declared further down, or with a prefix of your choosing - start the expression with a declare namespace line:
A declaration applies only to its own expression.
div.h4: Inserting the location of a node
div.p: To start from a node in the XML file, put the cursor on it - on an element or an attribute - and press ⌥G / Alt+G (XML: Add XPath Location to Queries). Its location, such as /orders/order[2]/@id, is added to the end of the query file, with the cursor on it, ready to run or change. If it's already in the query file, the cursor moves to it. With the cursor on no node, the query file is just opened.

In the query file, at the start of an expression, the same location is offered by auto-completion - type /, or press ⌃Space / Ctrl+Space. It's the first suggestion, marked cursor in orders.xml. The XML file must be shown in an editor.

Above each expression, on the blank line before it, is ▶ Run on orders.xml, naming the XML file it runs on. Click it to run the expression, or press ⌘Enter / Ctrl+Enter to run the expression at the cursor. The text in the XML file's editor is used, including any changes not yet saved.
div.aside: With no blank line before an expression, e.g. on the first line, ▶ Run is a CodeLens above it - or, with CodeLens turned off (editor.codeLens), at the start of the expression's line.
div.p: If Saxon reports an error, such as a syntax error, it's shown in the Problems panel, at the place in the expression where Saxon found it.
After each expression run, its result is shown in brief, at the end of its last line:

ul.li: → /orders/order[1]/@id (1 of 3) - the location of the first node found, and how many there are
= 3, or = ('pen', 'ink', 'pad') - values, written as XPath literals and cut short if they're long

div.p: Click it to see the whole result in the XPath Query output panel, with each item on a line of its own. A map, array or function is written on one line, e.g. map{"a":[1,"two",true()]} or fn:count#1 - to see part of a large map, change the expression to select it.

When the result has nodes, the XML file's editor shows the first, with the nodes listed beside it, as VS Code lists references. Click one to go to it, or press F4 / ⇧F4 to go to the next or previous node. The name of an element or attribute is selected, and for a text node, its text.
div.aside: At most 5000 items of a result are shown.
div.p: Expressions run on the XML file you were last in. Click into another XML file's editor, and ▶ Run names that file: run the same expressions on it, as you would search it with Find. The checks and auto-completion in the query file follow the switch, for the new file's names and namespaces.
The results shown after the expressions are those for the file they'd run on. Switch back to an earlier file to see its results again.
This is separate from the XML context file shown in the status bar for Quick Run and tasks: switching between XML files doesn't change it.

ul.li: Each run starts Java, so it takes about a second.
Results shown after the expressions aren't kept when VS Code is closed.
